# Kushmanda v2 — constrained decoding for identifiers (RP-44)

737 held-out questions whose answer is one identifier: the same seed-7 sample as the training report. The same model answers each question twice. **Free** decoding is as in [kushmanda.md](kushmanda.md). In **constrained** decoding the model may only write an identifier present in its passages, and cites the passage that contains it. If it declines freely, the abstention stands.

| Question and measure | Free | Constrained | Word overlap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Technique ID by name — exact match | 0.528 | 0.604 | 0.962 |
| Technique ID by name — cited the right passage | 0.736 | 0.604 | 0.962 |
| Behaviour → technique — exact match | 0.423 | 0.432 | 0.690 |
| No passage holds the answer — declined | 0.403 | 0.403 | 0.000 |
| Valid outputs (an identifier or a declining) | 0.993 | 1.000 | — |

## How to read this

- Constraining guarantees the **form**: every output is an identifier the evidence contains, with a consistent citation, or a refusal. It cannot make the model **choose** the right one. The remaining gap to word overlap is in choosing.
- The declining row covers only this ID-question subset, so it differs from the all-questions rate in [kushmanda.md](kushmanda.md).
- So in serving, the identifier comes from retrieval, and the model writes the explanation around it.
- Run on `cuda` in 83.9 s; weights are the private Kaggle Model `sati-kushmanda` v2.
